 Filipino MSMEs drive Shopee's 11.11 holiday sales growth 
 Close menu 
 November 20, 2026 
 1:08PM PHT
 Holiday spending 
 Shopee 
 Share
 Insider Spotlight 
 Filipino micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) accounted for 66 percent of Shopee's order growth during its 11.11 Mega Pamasko Sale 
 Six in 10 orders came from small businesses, with MSME orders surging 119 percent compared to an average day 
 Shopee Video checkouts increased 30 percent year-on-year as shoppers increasingly turned to video content before purchasing 
 Filipino micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) emerged as major contributors to Shopee's 11.11 Mega Pamasko Sale, highlighting the growing role of local businesses in capturing consumer spending during the holiday shopping season.
 According to Shopee, MSMEs contributed 66 percent of the platform's overall order growth during the campaign, while six in 10 orders came from small businesses. MSME orders also jumped 119 percent compared to an average day. 
 Access to a wider consumer base 
 The figures underscore how major online shopping campaigns provide Filipino entrepreneurs with opportunities to expand their customer base and compete alongside established international brands. 
 With thousands of MSMEs operating on Shopee, the platform gives smaller merchants access to a wider consumer market, particularly during peak shopping periods when demand for holiday purchases increases. 
 11.11 sees six in 10 orders come from MSMEs, as shoppers come in early through ShopeeVIP and turn to Shopee Video.| Contributed photo 
 Video-driven product discovery 
 Consumer shopping habits are also shifting toward early purchases, membership benefits, and video-driven product discovery. 
 ShopeeVIP members were among the earliest shoppers during the campaign, taking advantage of membership benefits such as daily 20 percent discount vouchers, free-shipping discounts, and priority customer service. 
 Meanwhile, checkouts through Shopee Video increased 30 percent year-on-year, reflecting growing consumer interest in product demonstrations and seller engagement before making purchasing decisions. 
 Vincent Lee  
 Shopee Philippines head  
 Shopee Philippines head  Vincent Lee  said the changing shopping behavior presents opportunities for local merchants to strengthen their online presence and generate sales. 
 “Holiday shopping in the Philippines is becoming far more visual, deliberate, and value-driven,” Lee said in a press statement. 
 “Shoppers want to stretch their budgets through programs like ShopeeVIP while seeing products in action via Shopee Video. And Filipino MSMEs have been quick to meet that demand. Our role is to keep lowering the barriers so local sellers can turn that engagement into sustainable growth through 11.11 and beyond,” he added.   —Vanessa Hidalgo | Ed: Corrie S. Narisma
